prize_parts.citation: For the rational design of molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pore architectures and active sites

statement.case_for: Zeolite and molecular-sieve design is the clearest case on the shortlist of structure determining function and then being exploited by design. Structure-directing agents (Zones), new and extra-large-pore frameworks (Davis) and catalyst design for cracking, selective conversion and emission control (Corma) form one coherent, original body of work with decades of independent confirmation and very large industrial deployment. It is also a field in which structure solution from tiny crystals was decisive, and the structural evidence is unambiguous, which is the standard I apply to every candidate.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is timing and optics. The 2025 prize went to metal-organic frameworks, so a second porous-materials prize immediately afterwards may look like a repeat of the same theme, and some will argue that zeolite catalysis is incremental engineering of a mature material class. The field is also broad, so the three-person cut (excluding Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis, and arguably others) is contestable, and the line between discovery and engineering is blurry. My own proximity to zeolite structure work means I should discount my enthusiasm.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks sequencing by synthesis (B011) first as a simple, chemistry-driven idea with exceptionally broad consequences, and values perovskites in the spirit of the MOF prize.
responses.response: I agree that Balasubramanian and Klenerman present the cleanest chemical invention among the high-impact candidates, and I treat B011 as a serious contender. My reservation is whether the committee wants a sequencing prize to read as chemistry rather than biology, and that depends on the citation wording. On perovskites I disagree with the 'spirit of the MOF prize' argument. A new material with fast efficiency gains is attractive, but operational stability and lead toxicity are unresolved, so I would hold B005 as an alternative rather than lead with it.

responses.point: Chabes places targeted protein degradation (B034) first because it turns ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction, via PROTACs and thalidomide-type glues acting through cereblon.
responses.response: The mechanism is well defined and I accept that it is a real conceptual advance. I am less convinced it is ready. No approved PROTAC drug is established, and the credit is split between the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands with eight credited names against a three-person limit, so any trio will leave out people whose contributions were decisive. I would want that allocation to be convincingly resolved before supporting it over a field with decades of confirmed impact.

responses.point: Somfai puts Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B053) first for its ligand-controlled generality, mechanistic clarity and ubiquitous use in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, with Buchwald and Hartwig as clear laureates.
responses.response: This is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and Somfai is right that two names and a stable mechanism make it easy to defend. I would still put design of structure-defined catalysts ahead of it, because the molecular-sieve work explains selectivity through pore geometry that can be verified crystallographically. I do not regard the two as exclusive. If the committee prefers a prize with simple attribution, B053 is a legitimate competitor to B051, and it is the case where my own field gives me no reason to overweight.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks long-range electron transfer through proteins (B028) first, as a quantitative physical mechanism confirmed for more than three decades, with Gray and Winkler as a clean two-name configuration.
responses.response: I respect the rigour of the Gray and Winkler work and agree it is mature and textbook. My question is breadth: it is a mechanism established in a defined set of proteins, whereas the molecular-sieve work changed what could be made and used. I would not oppose B028 on evidence, but I would need to be persuaded that its reach beyond bioinorganic physical chemistry is comparable. The recusal point in my conflict note concerns him as a Stockholm University colleague, not this candidate.

uncertainties: Whether the committee would accept a second porous-materials prize immediately after the 2025 MOF prize.
Whether the cut should be Corma, Davis, Zones or include Jihong Yu or Tsapatsis, and whether synthesis and catalysis credit is split correctly.
Whether sequencing by synthesis (B011) or protein degradation (B034) will be judged to offer a cleaner chemistry story with simpler attribution than my preferred candidate.
statement.conflict_note: Possible conflict: my research is on electron crystallography and structure determination of zeolites and other porous materials, and I work in a Stockholm University unit where the candidates' field is close to mine. I am also a Stockholm University colleague of Peter Brzezinski. I have no specific personal or institutional tie to Corma, Davis or Zones that is apparent from my profile, but I flag the proximity so the committee can decide whether recusal on B051 is warranted.
